question: At its October 30, 2026 meeting, will the FDA Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee vote in favor of SYD-101 (atropine 0.01%) for pediatric progressive myopia?

calls.reasoning: Base: adcoms side with FDA briefing ~75-80%; FDA's division already issued a CRL saying effectiveness not supported, giving a ~35-40% prior for a favorable vote. Updates up: prespecified FDA-agreed primary endpoint met (p=0.023) plus key secondary (p=0.0002), no safety/CMC deficiencies, no approved US therapy, widespread compounded use, EU/UK approval, benefit-risk framing favors approval when risk is minimal, and the adcom arose from a formal dispute resolution (suggesting the dispute office sees merit). Updates down: small absolute effect (~0.21 D over 3 yrs), no dose-response (0.03% worse than 0.01%), no axial length endpoint, a likely negative FDA briefing, and Vyluma's 0.01% NVK002 also failed to win approval. No human market found.
calls.dossier:
- Meeting confirmed: DODAC Oct 30, 2026, 8:30-15:00 ET, NDA 219694, docket FDA-2026-N-10606, includes Open Public Hearing (Federal Register 2026-09-25; FDA calendar). FDA 2026 materials page (current as of 09/24/2026) lists only the announcement; no briefing docs or voting questions posted as of Oct 19 (they typically post ~2 business days before).
- CRL Oct 23, 2025: FDA acknowledged STAR met primary endpoint but said data 'do not support the effectiveness of low-dose atropine in children with myopia'; reviewers noted no safety or product-quality deficiencies (pharmacytimes/ophthalmologymanagement, Oct-Nov 2025).
- Sydnexis filed Formal Dispute Resolution Request with Office of Specialty Medicine; July 2026 FDA announced intent to convene adcom (optometrytimes, glance 2026-07-28).
- STAR: 847 children aged 3-14; primary = proportion with confirmed progression beyond -0.75 D at Month 36, p=0.0226; key secondary annual progression rate p=0.0002; the -0.75D threshold was identified as clinically meaningful by the 2003 DODAC and FDA agreed to its use (company materials).
- Mean SE change at 36 mo: 0.01% -0.71 D, 0.03% -0.76 D, vehicle -0.92 D, i.e. ~0.21 D difference for 0.01% and no dose-response (higher dose worse) (clinicaltrialsarena, Nov 2025). Company: >50% reduction in fast progressors (>-0.5D/yr) subgroup, which is post hoc.
- Expert commentary (Healio 2026-10-07): the lack of an axial length endpoint 'hurt Sydnexis'; FDA may have questioned the clinical meaningfulness of averages; experts value a stabilized, FDA-regulated product over compounded atropine.
- No FDA-approved myopia drug in the US; compounded low-dose atropine is widely used; SYD-101 approved in EU/UK as Ryjunea (Santen).
- Precedent: Vyluma NVK002 (atropine 0.01%, CHAMP) NDA accepted 2023 with PDUFA Jan 31, 2024; it has not been approved in the US (no approval found).
- Base rates: adcom votes agree with the FDA's eventual action/briefing stance ~75-80% (general literature, over all drug adcoms); favorable votes despite a skeptical FDA briefing are less common but not rare, especially for benefit-risk questions with benign safety.
- Status quo: no approved product; FDA division on record as negative.
- Resolution: resolves off the official FDA voting tally for the benefit-risk/approval question (latest such vote); a tie = NO; no approval-oriented vote = annulled.
- Event window: single meeting on Oct 30, 2026; as of Oct 19 the meeting has not occurred (0% of window elapsed).
- Searched but not found: panel roster, voting question wording, FDA briefing document, any prediction market (none on Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi found).
calls.reference_class: FDA drug advisory committee votes where the FDA review division had previously issued a CRL / briefing skeptical of efficacy

calls.reasoning: Base rate: AC votes are positive ~60% overall, lower (~35-45%) when the FDA already issued a CRL and holds a skeptical view. Pro: STAR met primary (p=0.023) and key secondary (p=0.0002) endpoints, benign safety through M48, EU/UK approval, widespread off-label clinical use, strong clinician advocacy, AC convened after the formal dispute; a benefit-risk vote favors a safe drug with modest benefit. Con: small mean effect (0.30 vs 0.38 D/yr), no axial length endpoint, FDA's CRL wording reads as class-level skepticism about low-dose atropine (Vyluma's 0.01% product also got a CRL in 2024), and the FDA briefing may frame the effect as not clinically meaningful. Market check: no Polymarket/Manifold/Kalshi market found.
calls.dossier:
- STAR Phase 3 (847 children aged 3-14, US+EU): primary endpoint (proportion with confirmed progression of -0.75 D or worse at M36) met, p=0.0226 (139 vehicle vs 111 on 0.01%); key secondary annual progression rate -0.30 D/yr on 0.01% vs -0.38 D/yr vehicle, p=0.0002; no new safety signals through M48 (Optometry Times / Ophthalmology Times, 2025-2026).
- AAPOS 2026 (reviewofmm, Mar-Apr 2026): ages 3-12 subgroup showed a 47.9% reduction at M12, 37.6% at M24, 28.0% at M36; fast progressors with mild-moderate myopia showed a 56.9% reduction at M36 (p=0.0004); ages 13-14 had minimal progression regardless of treatment. These are post-hoc/subgroup analyses.
- CRL dated 2025-10-23: FDA acknowledged the primary endpoint was met but said the data do not support the effectiveness of low-dose atropine in children with myopia; no safety or CMC (manufacturing quality) issues were cited.
- Sydnexis filed a Formal Dispute Resolution Request with the FDA Office of Specialty Medicine; in July 2026 FDA announced it would convene an AC. The Federal Register notice (2026-09-25) covers DODAC on Oct 30, 2026, NDA 219694, docket FDA-2026-N-10606; briefing materials are due no later than 2 business days before the meeting. The voting questions were not yet public as of Oct 19.
- Healio (2026-10-07): experts suggest FDA questioned whether the averaged reduction is clinically meaningful; the lack of an axial length endpoint hurt Sydnexis, and regulators now expect it. Experts expect a deeper look and possible approval with age-restricted labeling.
- Precedent: Vyluma's NVK002 (atropine 0.01%, CHAMP trial, 576 children, primary efficacy shown) received a CRL in 2024 (Market Scope / reviewofmm). This suggests consistent FDA skepticism about the drug class.
- SYD-101 is approved in the EU/UK (Santen, Ryjunea; positive CHMP opinion April 2025).
- Low-dose atropine is widely used via compounding by US pediatric ophthalmologists and optometrists; there is strong clinician advocacy and an Open Public Hearing is scheduled.
- Base rates: FDA AC votes are positive roughly 60% across all drugs (general knowledge, not looked up this run). For applications with a prior CRL and an FDA reviewer position against effectiveness, the positive rate is lower (rough estimate, not a published figure).
- Status quo: the FDA's current position is that effectiveness is not demonstrated.
- Resolves off the official FDA vote tally on the overall benefit-risk/approval question (latest such vote); a tie counts as NO; no such vote means annulment. An effectiveness-only voting question is a possible framing risk.
- Event window: the meeting on 2026-10-30 (8:30am-3pm ET); as of 2026-10-19 the meeting has not occurred.

calls.reference_class: FDA advisory committee votes on drugs that previously received a CRL despite meeting the primary endpoint, convened after a dispute

calls.reasoning: Prior from FDA adcoms where the agency's own review is negative (post-CRL): sponsors win roughly 20-35%. Up-adjusted because the risk side is near zero (benefit-risk framing favours Yes if any benefit is accepted), real unmet need, EU/UK approval, practising clinicians on the panel, a lobbying petition, and the adcom arising from a formal dispute resolution request (suggests a close call). Held below 50% because the FDA's efficacy concerns are substantive: overall effect <10%, sensitivity to imputation, waning effect, no stop-vs-continue difference, axial length not significant (p=0.076), and literature suggesting 0.01% is the weakest dose. No human prediction market found (checked Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi via search; none). Briefing docs not yet posted as of Oct 19.
calls.dossier:
- CRL issued Oct 23, 2025: FDA acknowledged the STAR primary endpoint was met (p=0.0226; key secondary annual progression p=0.0002) but said the data 'did not support the effectiveness' of low-dose atropine. The CRL listed 5 concerns: (1) overall treatment effect <10%; (2) significance could be lost with small shifts in imputed values; (3) efficacy declining over time; (4) no meaningful difference between children who continued vs discontinued; (5) generalizability to the US population. No safety or CMC issues were cited (mediamice.com, 2025-26).
- Fast-progressor subgroup (>=0.5 D/yr): 0.425 D difference at 36 months; relative reductions of 76%/65%/57% at 12/24/36 months. Axial length separation 0.08 mm at 24 months, p=0.076 (not significant) (mediamice).
- Healio, Oct 7, 2026: pediatric experts said the lack of an axial-length endpoint 'hurt Sydnexis' and that the FDA questioned clinical meaningfulness of averages; experts were optimistic that subgroup data could show value.
- Glance, Jul 28, 2026: the adcom was convened after Sydnexis's Formal Dispute Resolution Request to the Office of Specialty Medicine; Sydnexis asked for practising pediatric ophthalmologists and optometrists on the panel; >1,000 US eye-care providers signed a petition supporting reconsideration.
- Federal Register, Sep 25, 2026: DODAC meeting notice for NDA 219694, indication 'slowing of myopia progression in children 3 years and older'; docket FDA-2026-N-10606; includes an Open Public Hearing.
- The same product is approved in the EU and UK as Ryjunea (Santen). No FDA-approved drug for pediatric myopia exists; US clinicians use compounded atropine.
- Comparator: Vyluma NVK002 (atropine 0.01%, CHAMP trial) also received FDA CRL(s) (original action date Jan 2024; another CRL in June 2024 per AdisInsight). This is a pattern of FDA's ophthalmology division being skeptical of low-dose atropine.
- FDA meeting-materials page as of Oct 19: only the announcement is posted; the briefing docs and voting questions are not yet posted (typically ~2 business days before the meeting).
- Base rates: across all FDA adcoms, votes favour the product roughly 60-70% of the time. For adcoms where FDA's briefing is negative or a CRL preceded, sponsor-favourable votes are much rarer (roughly 20-35%, rough literature recollection, not verified this run).

calls.reference_class: FDA advisory committee votes on applications where FDA had previously issued a CRL / briefing is negative on efficacy

calls.reasoning: Prior ~35-40% for a sponsor win when the FDA division has issued a CRL questioning effectiveness. Upward: prespecified FDA-agreed primary (p=0.023) and key secondary (p=0.0002) met, essentially no safety/CMC risk so a benefit-risk vote favors Yes if any benefit is accepted, no approved US therapy, widespread compounded use, EU/UK approval, and the adcom arose from a formal dispute (signals a close call). Downward: small mean effect (~0.21 D over 3 years, <10% overall effect), no dose-response, axial length not significant, imputation fragility, waning effect, a likely negative FDA briefing, and the FDA's same skepticism toward Vyluma's 0.01% atropine. Net roughly a coin flip, tilted slightly to Yes by the benefit-risk framing.
calls.reconciliation: The runs (0.45-0.56) disagreed mainly on judgment: how strongly a benign-safety benefit-risk question offsets an FDA division on record against effectiveness. Factual checks: (1) whether the briefing documents or voting questions were posted. Searches found none, consistent with the 2-business-day posting rule. (2) Vyluma NVK002 status: Drugs.com confirms it is still not FDA approved and was in post-PDUFA back-and-forth in 2024. This supports class-level FDA skepticism but is not new. (3) Panel roster: nothing found. With no factual dispute left to break the tie, I take a near coin flip tilted slightly to Yes because a benefit-risk question on a near-zero-risk drug with unmet need tends to draw Yes votes. That is offset by the substantive efficacy concerns (small effect, imputation fragility, no dose-response) that a statistically minded panel and an FDA briefing will stress. I carried Run 3's reference class forward, with a base rate near 0.38.
